    ut_add_symbol_prefix()

    UDUNITS-2 Documentation ut_add_symbol_prefix()

    Adds a symbolic prefix and scale factor to a unit system.

    Prototype

    int ut_add_symbol_prefix(
    ut_system* system,
    const char* symbol,
    double value
);

    Header

    #include <udunits2.h>

    Description

    Adds a symbol-based prefix to a unit system.

    This function registers a prefix identified by a short symbol (e.g., "k") and associates it with a numeric scale factor (e.g., 1000). Once added, the prefix can be used in unit parsing and formatting within the specified ut_system.

    For example, after adding the prefix "k" with value 1e3, expressions such as "km" can be parsed as "k" applied to "m".

    The prefix represents a multiplicative scale factor and does not impose any dimensional constraints on units.

    The prefix is only recognized during parsing operations that use this specific ut_system instance. Prefix definitions are not shared between systems and do not affect parsing in other ut_system instances.

    Parameters

    Parameter Description
    system Pointer to the unit system to which the prefix will be added. Must be a valid, initialized ut_system and not NULL
    symbol The symbol of the prefix (e.g., "k"). Must be a non-NULL, non-empty string
    value The numeric scale factor associated with the prefix (e.g., 1e3 for kilo). Must be a finite, non-zero value

    Returns

    Return Value Description
    0 Success. The prefix was added to the system
    UT_EXISTS A prefix with the same symbol already exists in the system
    UT_BAD_ARG One or more arguments are invalid
    UT_OS A system-level error occurred (e.g., memory allocation failure)

    Preconditions

    • system must be a valid, initialized ut_system object.
    • symbol must be non-NULL and non-empty.
    • The prefix symbol should not already exist in the system.
    • value should be a finite, non-zero numeric scale factor.

    Error Handling

    Returns a non-zero value on failure. The specific error condition can be retrieved using ut_get_status().

    Object Ownership

    • The system object remains owned by the caller.
    • The function internally manages any storage associated with symbol; the caller retains ownership of the original string.
    • No new user-managed objects are returned.

    Thread Safety

    Not thread-safe.

    This function modifies the internal state of the ut_system. External synchronization is required when accessing or modifying a shared system.

    Example

    This example demonstrates how ut_add_symbol_prefix() registers the "k" prefix in a unit system, enabling parsing of prefixed units such as "km".

    #include <stdio.h>
#include <udunits2.h>

int main(void) {
    ut_system* system = ut_read_xml(NULL);
    if (!system) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize unit system\n");
        return 1;
    }

    if (ut_add_symbol_prefix(system, "k", 1e3) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to add symbol prefix\n");
        ut_free_system(system);
        return 1;
    }

    ut_unit* unit = ut_parse(system, "km", UT_UTF8);
    if (unit) {
        printf("Successfully parsed 'km'\n");
        ut_free(unit);
    } else {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to parse 'km'\n");
    }

    ut_free_system(system);
    return 0;
}
